No blocker found in the written minimal correction. No native edge minimum, board geometry, routing rule, supported outline shape, default-class admission or acceptance check changes.

The prior comprehension treated legitimate repeated layer definitions in the root setup/stackup as duplicate geometry selectors. Both paired001 arms actually failed with duplicate singleton layer after source-drc/export/obstacle stages and before an engine/JVM step. The actual source stackup has nine declarations, including surfaces, outer copper and dielectric. Both aggregate methods remain failed/unaccepted; their CPU/wall costs must remain charged to the continuation. This review does not rerun either method.

The correction locates only sx.one(board,setup)->sx.one(setup,stackup), skips that exact object by identity in the selector comprehension, and leaves `_walk` traversal unchanged. Its descendants are still traversed. Duplicate setup/stackup singleton declarations fail through existing sx.one. Nested or merely structurally equal stackup objects are not exempt. The change does not claim general stackup validation; retained original/native checks still govern it.

The new positive test uses a legitimate root stackup with repeated copper/dielectric declarations and asserts exact original rectangle bounds/edge hash/clearance plus byte-identical corrected DSN and new source binding. usability_review.text:
# Narrow usable-workflow documentation review

Read `START_HERE.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/routing-preferences.md` and
`docs/gui-workflow.md` against the actual CLI argument/dispatch definitions,
preferences API, engine installer, cancellation/acceptance code and the linked
installation/product scope notes. Every local Markdown link in these four
documents resolves. No tests, Native, JVM, network, Git, routing, source edits or
subagents were used. Only this excluded review directory is written.

**No broken documented command or release-blocking installation/acceptance claim
was identified in this static pass.** Route/preview overrides, selected-net
completion-only restrictions, settings starters, accept/reject intent, fresh
separate export/check, and Ctrl-C behavior agree with the implementation.
The new-checkout instructions explicitly reuse qualified existing Mac apps;
their installation scope notes do not claim a fresh OS or formal package.
GUI review remains a separate-project workflow without live apply/undo or
unsaved-buffer inspection. Historical qualification was read, not rerun.

Two small wording fixes would help the nontechnical owner:

1. **UF-1, P3 — Contradictory preset-write wording.**
   `docs/routing-preferences.md:32` says “The helper never writes a preset,”
   immediately after instructing use of `settings-init`. The CLI intentionally
   creates the requested preset exclusively (`autorouter/__main__.py:124-128`).
   Suggested wording: “Routing does not rewrite your preset or personal KiCad/
   Freerouting settings. `settings-init` creates only the explicit new file.”
   This is documentation ambiguity, not an implementation defect.
2. **UF-2, P3 — Scope the absolute warning sentence.**
   `START_HERE.md:18` says “All original warnings remain.” In context this may
   describe the cited measured circuits, but it could be read as a universal
   acceptance rule. Generic native acceptance preserves evidence/policy, not
   equality of every source/candidate warning; pruning permits a warning subset
   (`strategy.py:576`), and removing unprotected dangling copper can legitimately
   clear a routing warning. Suggested wording: “The cited comparisons retain
   their inherited warnings; source and final findings stay visible in evidence.”
   No cited numerical result is contradicted by this static observation.

The lead owns any wording integration after the running pair. This review
establishes CLI/document consistency only; it does not add fresh installation,
GUI, cancellation, native routing or human PCB qualification.
